---
title: "Release runbook"
date: 2026-11-24
date-modified: 2026-11-24
---

What a Bioconductor release roll asks of this platform, in the order it happens. Bioconductor
releases twice a year; each time, devel becomes the release and a new devel starts. This page
is kept up to date by whoever runs a release: change a step when it turns out wrong, and add
the cycle to the [log](#log) at the end.

Version numbers below are this cycle's: release 3.23 → 3.24, devel 3.24 → 3.25. Read
`<release>`, `<devel>` and `<next>` as the release, the devel and the next devel being rolled to.

## What moves on its own, and what doesn't

Most of the roll is driven by one file, `config.yaml` on
[Bioconductor/bioconductor.org](https://github.com/Bioconductor/bioconductor.org) `devel`,
which the core team edits. Everything listed here reads it, or reads something that does.

| Piece | Follows | How it learns |
|---|---|---|
| Package pages' release/devel chrome, canonicals, sitemap, search | `release_version`, `devel_version` | the astro build ([Astro site build](astro-site-build.qmd)) |
| `/config.yaml`, `/js/versions.js` | the same | the astro build |
| `/bioc-version`, `/bioc-devel-version` at the site root | master's copies, which nanoc writes from the same file | `bioc-sync`, hourly (the edge serves these two from the mirror, not the build) |
| `/packages/release/`, `/packages/devel/` | the served build's `bioc-version`, `bioc-devel-version` | the Worker, within 60 s of `site/latest` moving |
| `/checkResults/release/`, `/books/release/` and the other aliases | master's symlinks | `bioc-sync`, hourly |
| Which r-universe a version's package data comes from | each universe's `BiocVersion` | bioc-website `pipeline/packages.py` `universe_for()`, nightly |
| R version for a version not yet in `r_ver_for_bioc_ver` | the repository's binary indexes | `r_version_for()`, nightly |
| Registry gating R | `devel_version`/`release_version` → `r_ver_for_bioc_ver` | bioc-registry, at evaluate time |
| r-universe's `bioc` and `bioc-release` | `r_universe_devel_version`, `r_universe_release_version` | r-universe |
| Mirror manifests (`/api/v1/manifest/`) | master's symlinks | `gen-manifest.sh` |

What does **not** move on its own:

- **Adding the next devel's package data** to the snapshot ([step 3](#add-next)).
- **Retiring the old release** from the snapshot ([after the release](#after)).
- **The container-binaries redirect bound** in `packages/edge/worker/gen-redirects.ts`
  (`v <= 25` today). The release-roll guard ([ADR 0007](https://seandavi.github.io/bioc-infrastructure/adr/0007-cloudflare-workflows-for-the-release-roll-guard.html))
  alerts when devel passes it.
- **Getting a `devel` edit onto the site quickly.** `sync.yml`'s 30-minute schedule is
  throttled by GitHub to every few hours in practice (4–12 hours apart in November 2026).
  Dispatch it by hand ([below](#dispatch-sync)) whenever an edit is waiting.

## Before release day

### 1. The branch is cut

The core team creates `RELEASE_<x_y>` for the outgoing devel and seeds `packages/<next>/` on
master, partly as symlinks to `<devel>` (`packages/3.25/workflows/VIEWS -> ../../3.24/…`).

Check: `gh api repos/bioc/BiocVersion/branches --jq '.[].name'` lists `RELEASE_<x_y>`, and
`https://bioconductor.org/packages/<next>/bioc/VIEWS` returns 200.

### 2. r-universe rolls

The core team sets `r_universe_release_version` and `r_universe_devel_version` in
`config.yaml`. r-universe then rebuilds `bioc` from git `devel` (now `<next>`) and
`bioc-release` from `RELEASE_<x_y>`, each on its own schedule. Lori's edit for this cycle
reached the site seven hours late ([#195](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/195)),
so dispatch the sync as soon as it lands.

Check which version each universe serves:

```sh
for u in bioc bioc-release; do
  printf '%s ' $u; curl -s https://$u.r-universe.dev/api/packages/BiocVersion | jq -r '.Version + " " + .RemoteRef'
done
```

Nothing to do in the pipeline: each night it reads whichever universe's `BiocVersion` matches
the version it builds. A version neither universe serves (mid-roll, `<devel>` was in neither)
takes its software data from the source tarballs' DESCRIPTION, like the other three
repositories, and says so in the log (`no r-universe builds 3.24; software from --data-origin
tarballs`). Expect a few dozen fewer software pages for it until r-universe catches up: the
tarballs cover only packages in the repository's `PACKAGES`.

### 3. Add the next devel's package data {#add-next}

On onclappc02, from a bioc-website checkout at `main` (not the ops clone the timers run from):

```sh
DRY_RUN=1 ADD_RELEASE=<next> ops/refresh-packages.sh   # build and check, no upload
ADD_RELEASE=<next> ops/refresh-packages.sh             # upload, dispatch both builds
```

It takes the same snapshot lock as the timers, so it can't race them. Needs
`packages/<next>/bioc/bin/windows/contrib/<R>/PACKAGES` to exist (empty is fine) when
`config.yaml` has no `r_ver_for_bioc_ver` for `<next>` yet. **Don't** add one early: that map
is BiocManager's, and a version in it that is neither release nor devel is "out-of-date" to R
users. From then on the nightly `bioc-site-packages` refreshes `<next>` with the rest.

Check, once the astro build has published:

```sh
curl -s https://bioconductor.org/packages/<next>/bioc/html/limma.html | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g' | grep -o 'This package is for version [0-9.]*'
curl -s https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/html/limma.html | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g' | grep -o 'This is the [a-z]* version'   # still "development", for <devel>
```

`/packages/json/<next>/` stays 404 until release day: the legacy nanoc job on master writes
`packages.json` only for `config.yaml`'s `versions`.

## Release day

### 4. The core team edits `config.yaml`

On `devel`, in one commit: `release_version: "<devel>"`, `devel_version: "<next>"`,
`versions: ["<devel>", "<next>"]`, `r_ver_for_bioc_ver` gains `"<next>": "<R>"`,
`release_dates` gains `"<devel>": "<mm/dd/yyyy>"`, and the R versions, `devel_repos` and
`single_package_builder` as the file's own `CHANGE THIS` comments say. The astro build checks
the pair is consistent (`devel_version` must be the version after `release_version`).

### 5. Get it onto the site {#dispatch-sync}

```sh
gh workflow run sync.yml -R seandavi/bioconductor.org --ref astro
```

The sync merges `devel` into `astro`, runs the checks and dispatches `astro.yml`. About five
minutes end to end on 2026-11-24 (sync under 3 min, build and publish 3–8 min). The Worker sees the
new `site/latest` within 60 s, and with it the new `/packages/release/` and `/packages/devel/`.

### 6. Verify

```sh
curl -s https://bioconductor.org/bioc-version; echo; curl -s https://bioconductor.org/bioc-devel-version; echo
curl -sI https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/limma.html | grep -i x-bioc-build
curl -s https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/limma.html | sed 's/<[^>]*>//g' | grep -o 'Bioconductor [0-9.]* Software' | head -1
curl -s https://bioconductor.org/config.yaml | grep -E '^(release|devel)_version'
```

The last two should show the new pair as soon as the build is served, and `x-bioc-build`
should be the id in `site/latest`. `/bioc-version` and `/bioc-devel-version` are master's
copies from the mirror, so they show the new pair only after master's nanoc rebuild and the
next hourly sync; `/packages/release/` follows the build's own copies straight away.

### 7. Watch for

- **The release-roll guard.** If devel passed the redirect bound, the `bioc-release-roll`
  Workflow alerts and waits for approval. Raise the bound in `gen-redirects.ts`, run
  `just redirects`, and deploy the Worker.
- **The registry.** Its gating R follows `devel_version` → `r_ver_for_bioc_ver`, so it moves to
  `<next>`'s R when step 4 lands. The dashboard's "why are packages not propagated?" panel
  names the gating R.
- **Master's symlinks.** `checkResults/`, `books/` and the mirror manifests follow master, which
  the legacy job flips on its own schedule.

## After the release {#after}

- **Retire the old release from the snapshot** once nothing links to it as live: drop its
  `data/<old>` from `_ci/site-data.tar.zst` (not scripted yet). It is then archival and served
  from the mirror ([ADR 0006](https://seandavi.github.io/bioc-infrastructure/adr/0006-old-releases-and-their-checkresults-are-archival.html)).
- **Update this page**, and add the cycle to the log.

## Log {#log}

### 3.24 (November 2026)

- **2026-11-24.** Lori Kern's `config.yaml` edit (`r_universe_*` to 3.24/3.25, devel commit
  `76f949fb`, 10:58 UTC) hadn't reached the site at 13:27 UTC: the scheduled sync last ran at
  06:46 UTC. Dispatched by hand at 13:39; live at 13:44
  ([#195](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/195)).
- Found, the same day, that the build took release/devel from the newest snapshot directory,
  and the pipeline picked r-universe by `devel_version` while r-universe had already moved
  `bioc` to 3.25. Fixed before any 3.25 data landed:
  [seandavi/bioconductor.org#22](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor.org/pull/22)
  (release/devel from `config.yaml`),
  [seandavi/bioc-website#86](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-website/pull/86) (universe by
  `BiocVersion`, `ADD_RELEASE`), [#208](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/pull/208)
  (Worker aliases follow the served build; redirect bound to 3.25).
- Release-day rehearsal, locally on the same data: one `config.yaml` edit flipped every package
  page, canonical and `bioc-version`, and every build check passed.
